decisions.reason: As a recent extension of the core authentication and secure communication offering in a growing market, it fits our capabilities and there is no clear performance shortfall yet that would justify withdrawing it.

The mobile PDF digital signature function is close to our established business and supports the firm's move toward secure cross-channel signing, so with no negative evidence we would retain it while results are still forming.

This multi-layer end-to-end security architecture builds directly on our R&D and cryptography strengths and is strategically aligned with customer demand for integrated high-assurance solutions, so it remains worth supporting.

The secure email-to-app delivery tool complements our trusted second-channel communication logic and broad solution portfolio, and a medium-sized firm with ongoing R&D would usually give such a new adjacent product more time before reallocating resources.

The QR-code-based hardware signature token is close to our existing hardware-enabled security competence and can serve regulated customers with stronger authentication needs, so absent evidence of underperformance we would keep it.

The payment network security compliance suite leverages our security and compliance expertise in an expanding digitalisation environment, and without a visible gap below aspiration levels there is no strong behavioral reason to drop it after only one year.
